data.narrative:
Chariot Defense is a Series A-stage defense and security company that has raised $41M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 4 private-market peers in the same sector and stage (Stark Defence, Castelion, Singularity, and NODA AI), supplemented by reference to 2 public defense contractors and additional private frontier-tech firms.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a valuation proxy, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yielding $82M. Peer-median analysis across the 4 same-stage, same-sector comparables produced a median valuation of $700M, though the sample is wide-ranging ($125M to $4.0B), reflecting significant dispersion in defensibility and market position within this cohort. The stage-progression method treats raised capital as a floor; the peer-median method anchors to realized market outcomes for direct competitors.

The triangulated valuation range is $70M (floor) to $805M (ceiling), with a median of $391M across the two methods. This wide band reflects material uncertainty around Chariot's competitive positioning relative to the peer set. Key variables not present in available data—revenue run rate, customer concentration, technology defensibility, and management track record relative to peers—would be required to narrow the range materially. The peer-median result should be weighted against the composition of the comp set, as valuations within it span nearly two orders of magnitude.
